detailed_analysis:
This is an in-situ synchrotron powder-XRD frame during a dehydration ramp (x = 2-theta in degrees). A single global fit of 17 split pseudo-Voigt peaks on a SNIP background over 5-45 deg achieves global R^2 = 0.99999 and peak_region_r2 = 0.9993 - an excellent description of positions and integrated intensities. Reflections are located at 5.10, 7.93, 11.94, 15.95, 17.93, 18.86, 19.99, 20.89, 21.41, 23.32, 24.03, 26.27, 26.98, 28.17, 29.50, 32.98, and 36.64 deg. The dominant intense lines (11.94 and 19.99 deg, amplitudes 1.4e6 and 1.1e6) carry most of the diffracted intensity.

Residual analysis: the normalized residuals are noise-like across most of the pattern but show sharp bipolar (derivative-shaped) excursions reaching ~40 sigma at the apices of the three sharpest/strongest lines (~11.9, ~17.7, ~20 deg). Per the domain validation rules this is the irreducible apex/asymmetry limit of the split-PV model on very high-count lines, NOT an unmodelled reflection; it should be accepted rather than chased with sub-window symmetric fits. The 17.5-17.9 deg region is correctly modelled as two overlapping components (peak_5 shoulder + peak_5/peak_7 vicinity).

Crystallite size: instrumental_fwhm was set to 0.0, so every Scherrer size is a LOWER BOUND (broadening is an upper bound). Per-peak Scherrer sizes span 7.5-31.7 nm - a >3x spread, which per the domain rules signals anisotropic (hkl-dependent) broadening rather than a single isotropic domain size; an isotropic mean (~25 nm) is an oversimplification. The 7.5 nm value (peak_1 at 5.1 deg, FWHM ~1.06 deg) and the ~15-17 nm values (peak_5, peak_15) are broad/weak or overlapped features and are the least reliable. The typical well-defined reflections cluster around 26-32 nm (lower bound).

Williamson-Hall: R^2 = 0.16 (far below the 0.7 threshold) and the slope is negative (-0.019, implying unphysical negative strain). Per the mandatory rules the W-H decomposition MUST NOT be reported - a negative/near-zero slope with poor linearity indicates uncorrected instrumental broadening (instrumental_fwhm=0), background/peak-assignment effects, or anisotropy. Fall back to the per-peak Scherrer range.

Several eta values are pinned at the 0 (pure Gaussian) or ~1 (pure Lorentzian) limits, meaning the Gaussian-Lorentzian mixing is not well constrained for those peaks; the split-FWHM asymmetry parameters are more informative than eta here. Since this is an in-situ variable-temperature run, peak positions/lattice will genuinely shift frame-to-frame - so any comparison across the ramp should track these centers as physical (the legitimate VT exception to the 'lattice should not move' prior).

scientific_claims.claim: The crystalline phase present in this dehydration-ramp frame shows anisotropic size broadening, with per-reflection coherent-domain sizes spanning ~7.5-32 nm (lower bounds; instrumental broadening not subtracted), most well-defined reflections implying >=26-32 nm; an isotropic Scherrer mean (~25 nm) is not physically justified.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Anisotropic domain size / hkl-dependent broadening in an in-situ dehydration series constrains how the crystallite morphology and defect structure evolve as water leaves the lattice, which single-number size reports would hide.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone observed anisotropic (hkl-dependent) crystallite-size broadening in a material undergoing in-situ dehydration by synchrotron powder XRD?

model_type: Sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt peaks on SNIP background (snip_iterations=auto), single global fit_pattern with auto peak detection (prominence_frac=0.01, min_distance_deg=0.10, eta free per peak, FWHM in [0.05,2.0]); fit_range lo raised above the dominant ~3.9 deg low-angle Bragg feature (lo=5.0, hi=45.0). Scherrer K=0.9, instrumental_fwhm=0.0 -> sizes are lower-bound (broadening upper-bound).

verification_iterations.model: Sum of split (asymmetric) pseudo-Voigt profiles on a SNIP background, fitted over a range with lo raised above the dominant ~3.9° low-angle feature. Confirmed real reflections to model (all above the giant feature, sitting on flat background): ~11.9°, the 17.5-17.9° region, and ~20.0°, plus any faint high-angle reflections (25-45°) auto-detected. The 17.1-18.4° region shows genuine two-sign-change structure (shoulder near ~17.55° on the low-angle side of the ~17.85° main peak) → fit as two overlapping pseudo-Voigt components jointly. eta in [0,1] per peak.

issues.problem: Under-resolved asymmetric feature: the data shows a shoulder rising to ~410000 near x≈17.85 that the single split-pseudo-Voigt cannot fully capture, leaving a ±25000 (55σ) oscillation.
Sharp intense apex (~1.6e6 counts) leaves a localized derivative-like residual (~40σ), typical of an irreducible apex/asymmetry on a very high-dynamic-range line.
